facts.text: East Elmhurst became a haven for African American homebuyers in the 1960s, one of few NYC areas where they could purchase houses.
The neighborhood’s streets honor civil rights leaders, and annual parades and murals celebrate that legacy.
The Langston Hughes Community Library and Cultural Center, designed by local residents, houses one of the largest collections of African American art and literature.
In 1904, the Bankers' Land and Mortgage Corporation launched a residential development that laid out about 2,000 lots, officially naming the area East Elmhurst.
Bowery Bay Beach, later North Beach, operated from 1886 until 1929 when it was razed to create a 105‑acre flying field.
75th Street and 31st Avenue was co‑named “Mount Everest Way” in 2019 to honor the Nepali American community.
